nodes.description: Thrombopoietin cannot signal through MPL on megakaryocyte-lineage cells and on hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells. MPL has no kinase activity of its own; ligand-induced receptor dimerization normally signals through JAK2 and STAT5 for proliferation and through sustained MAPK activation for differentiation. Serum thrombopoietin is markedly raised in every patient tested, consistent with a receptor defect rather than a ligand defect. CAMT iPSC studies show MPL signaling is needed both to keep the multipotent progenitor pool and to direct megakaryocyte-erythroid progenitors toward megakaryopoiesis. In CAMT iPSC-derived progenitors, restoring MPL produced aberrant megakaryocytes at the expense of erythropoiesis, which the authors trace to altered expression of the transcription factor FLI1, so MPL signaling also sets the megakaryocyte-versus-erythroid fate balance.

nodes.description: Not an established treatment. Null MPL alleles leave no receptor for these drugs to act on. In cell models, some missense receptors respond to an agonist that binds the transmembrane domain (the eltrombopag class) but not to thrombopoietin or to agonists that bind the extracellular domain, and the R464G receptor responded to eltrombopag only when mutant calreticulin was co-expressed. No clinical efficacy data in CAMT1 are available, and a pediatric review lists CAMT as a question for future study.
